label: paragraph_title
text: SINGAPORE MORTALITY STATISTICS.

label: text
text: The Singapore Municipal health statement for the week ending October 9, gives the total number of deaths as male 176, female 77. This represents "a death rate of 32.22 per mille per annum compared with 30.82 in the preceding week and 31.67 in the corresponding week last year. The chief causes of mortality were: Beriberi 13, phthisis 26, malaria 29, pneumonia 45, convulsions 18. Among the nationalities death occurred as follows: Europeans 2, Eurasians 3, Chinese 208, Malays 24, Indians 16. Twenty persons died who had been less than three months resident in Singapore. Deducting these the death rate was 29.67 per 1,000. The infantile rate was 227.2 per mille per annum compared with 221.9 in the preceding week and with 177.4 in the corresponding week of last year.

text: BACK BAY COMMITTEE'S REPORT

label: text
text: Simla, September 28.—The Government of India Bombay Back Bay Inquiry Committee have, at the instance of the Bombay Government, telegraphed from London an interim report to ensure work on the Bank Bay Reclamation scheme, unanimously recommending the reclamation of blocks one, two and eight by dredging or dry filling, which never is economical.

label: text
text: The Committee note that the area of the seventh block is $654,000$ square yards, and the quantity dredged and being filled with the exclusive murum topping required is $2,050,000$ cubic yards.

label: text
text: It is for the Local Government to decide upon action in respect of this block pending the decisions of the Government on the final report.

label: text
text: The Committee emphasise the necessity of taking immediate steps to find new and nearer quarries of murum, and arrange definitely for more abundant and speedier supplies at cheaper rates than at present.

label: paragraph_title
text: AID FOR LARGE FAMILIES.

label: text
text: The Government of New Zealand as introduced a family allowance ill, providing aid for large families 4th small incomes.

label: text
text:
It is proposed to pay two shillings weekly from State funds for each child, exceeding two, under 16 years of age, where the family income from all sources is less than $4 a week. The amounts are to be payable to mothers and the money must be applied for the benefit of the children.
The Minister of Pensions states that about fifty-five thousand children will be benefited at a cost of approximately a quarter of a million pounds annually.

label: paragraph_title
text: SMALL INCREASE.

label: text
text: London, Oct. 28.

label: text
text: An official report states that 262,000 miners are working to-day. The smallness of the net increase is due to appreciable local decreases, which are attributed to the feeling engendered by the banning of Mr. Cook's meetings.—Reuter.

label: text
text: Speaking at a meeting in his constituency (Epping) Mr. Winston Churchill indicated that the Government was ready to give the miners a final chance. He said that if the miners were prepared to make a proposal touching the real problems and difficulties, the Government was bound to consider

label: text
text: The question was not whether the owners could be got to agree, but whether the miners would make proposals and suggestions which the Government could endorse and carry forward irrespective of the opinions of the owners.

label: text
text: The Government offered an Arbitration Court which could override the owners. The offer was refused, and the Government had nothing more to say.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title
text: PROSECUTION

label: text
text: JUDGE REFUSES TO ORDER RE-TRIAL.

label: text
text: Singapore, October 19.—The Chief Justice (Sir William Murison) gave judgment this morning in a petition heard yesterday in which the Crown asked for no trial of

label: text
text: the Crown asked for, re-trial of v police court case in which Mrs. Georginn Howe was acquitted on a charge of recklessly driving a motor car.

label: text
text: The only ground for the petition, his Lordship said, was a statement by the magistrate, after he had decided the case, that he had since discovered that he had been misled by the prosecution wrongly reconstructing the case by means of diagram in court.

label: text
text: It appeared that the prosecution put up to the court a map on which the position of a lamp post was wrongly marked, and the error was discovered after the case had been decided.

label: text
text: His Lordship said he had grave doubts whether the power to order a re-trial was intended to be exercised in cases where the prosecution, entirely through their own fault, had failed to present their case properly.

label: text
text: If he complied with the petition he would be ordering that an acquitted person should be tried a second time for the reason that the prosecution had not launched all

label: text
text: prosecution had not launched all their available armoury at the first prosecution.

label: text
text: The civil rule was that a re-trial could only be ordered if evidence was available, which was not available at the time of the first prosecution.

label: text
text: His Lordship dismissed the petition.

label: paragraph_title
text: AN OLD KOREAN CUSTOM.

label: text
text: Tokyo, Oct. 9.—The quaint old Korean custom of carving a design on the neck of a girl who has jilted her sweetheart was frwned upon by the Tokyo Appeal Court when it sentenced Lyu Tetsufuku to 18 months' imprisonment for murderous assault on a girl in Moki, Korea.

label: text
text: Lyu's defence was that he had been engaged to the girl, but that she has found a handsome man and "given him the gate." He produced witnesses to prove that ancient Korean customs permitted him, under the circumstances, to

label: text
text: shave off her eyebrows or to cut a slice of skin from her neck. The Appeal Court ruled, however, that the carving custom, while undoubtedly most effective, had no standing in law and, consequently, Lyu was committed to prison.
